initial_sql_scope.unimplemented_behavior: explicit unsupported error; no silent success

oracle_semantics.reference_version: Oracle Database 19c documentation; no Oracle execution comparison
oracle_semantics.unquoted_identifier: ASCII uppercase; quoted bytes preserved; fixed PUBLIC namespace
oracle_semantics.empty_text: SQL Utf8 literal/bind inputs become typed NULL after type checking; native stored empty Utf8 and empty Binary remain values
oracle_semantics.uniqueness: Only all-NULL composite keys permit duplicates; validate statement-final delta in the engine
oracle_semantics.ddl: Entry syntax/support/session checks precede explicit prior-transaction commit; semantic validation and atomic native DDL follow only confirmed success
oracle_semantics.ddl_result: Separate prior_transaction_outcome and ddl_outcome, including NotAttempted and NotCommittedRecoveryRequired with per-transaction certainty; never retry the whole SQL automatically
oracle_semantics.isolation: DEV3-DESIGN-003 transaction snapshot plus table read/write-set validation; SQL READ COMMITTED exposure awaits actual native supply validation and a separate SQL decision
oracle_semantics.recovery: DEV3-DESIGN-003 WAL/persistent undo/CLR supply and rollback/recrash R1-R4; preserve NotCommitted/RecoveryRequired and fencing on incomplete undo; DEV2 private/COW is not disk execution evidence

prepared_execution.scope: DEV4 scalar types and DML/SELECT; embedded API first, DEV5 protocol, DEV6 clients

same transaction, statement rollback, quota and cancellation guarantees as direct execution
not_implied: shared plan cache or advanced reoptimization
array/batch binding, callable, LOB or XA support
open_before_implementation: D4-F01/F02: concrete Rust signatures and complete literal error/state vectors against actual DEV3 APIs
D4-F04/F05: worker protocol, fixed schedules, executable recipes and numerical performance/diagnostic budgets

design_choices.parameter_types: fixed at prepare using context or explicit hints; unresolved types rejected

design_choices.result_lifetime: one active result per session; bounded terminal token state; explicit close or EOF
